painting: Along the River During the Qingming Festival (清明上河圖), Zhang Zeduan, Northern Song, c. 1100s. Public domain.
tileNote: 8 tiles, each 3202x1200 (last one 3195), placed left to right = one continuous 25609x1200 image. The scroll is READ RIGHT-TO-LEFT: the story starts at the right end (tile 8, countryside) and ends at the left end (tile 1, the city).
coordinateNote: x and y are normalized 0-1 over the FULL stitched image (x=0 left edge, y=0 top). Hit radius suggestion: 0.015 in x, 0.12 in y.

chapters.title: 汴河 · The River
chapters.subtitle: From quiet countryside to the busy Bian River

chapters.title: 城門 · The City
chapters.subtitle: Through the gate into the capital Bianjing

targets.name: 驢隊 Donkey Caravan
targets.hint: At the very beginning, in the misty countryside
targets.story: The scroll opens at dawn: a small train of donkeys carrying charcoal walks toward the city. The whole painting follows this journey from quiet fields to the busiest city on Earth in 1100 AD.

targets.name: 漕船 Grain Barge
targets.story: The Bian River was the empire's artery. Barges like this carried grain from the south to feed about a million people in the capital.

targets.name: 帆船 Boat Under Tow
targets.hint: Out on the open water near the top
targets.story: Boatmen pulled vessels upstream with long ropes. Look closely: every rope, oar and wave is painted by hand.

targets.name: 彩樓歡門 Festive Gate
targets.hint: A tall bamboo structure beside a restaurant
targets.story: Restaurants built tall decorated bamboo gateways to attract customers. It was the Song dynasty's version of a neon sign.

targets.name: 虹橋 Rainbow Bridge
targets.hint: The dramatic heart of the scroll
targets.story: The most famous moment: a large boat is about to hit the arched bridge while crowds shout warnings. It is the painting's great climax, a single frozen second of chaos.

targets.name: 城門樓 City Gate Tower
targets.hint: The grand tower guarding the city
targets.story: Passing this gate you enter Bianjing (today's Kaifeng), then the largest and richest city in the world.

targets.name: 駱駝商隊 Camel Caravan
targets.hint: Travelers from the Silk Road near the gate
targets.story: Camels meant long-distance trade. Goods and ideas from Central Asia arrived through this very gate.

targets.name: 正店 Licensed Tavern
targets.hint: A sign with two characters on a busy street
targets.story: A 正店 was a licensed tavern allowed to brew its own wine, the most prestigious restaurants in the capital.

targets.name: 轎子 Sedan Chair
targets.story: Wealthy residents were carried through crowded streets in sedan chairs, a status symbol of the time.

targets.name: 牛車 Ox Cart
targets.hint: Heavy goods at the bottom of the street
targets.story: Oxen hauled heavy loads through the city. Nearly every person and animal in the scroll is doing a real job — over 800 people in total.
